summary: Engine: a card's own 'hindered from play' trigger (SelfRemovedFromPlayTrigger, method: hinder) is carried out as the player and the card that did the hindering, not as the hindered card and its owner. summary: Race Text 92_4: 'Fellowship: Play a pipe to play a pipeweed from your draw deck (or vice versa).' A card played from a draw deck onto a bearer, and an event played from one, shuffle the deck as the card leaves it (AttachPermanentAction, PlayEventAction: if playedFromZone == Zone.DECK, shuffleDeck). PlayPermanentAction, which plays a card to the support area or the table, does not, so the one shuffle is the definition's 'shuffle: true', and PlayCardFromDrawDeck carries that out after the whole stacked play, its triggers included. No definition can mend it: the engine would have to shuffle in PlayPermanentAction as the card leaves the deck, as the other two play actions do. Reaches every 'play ... from your draw deck' that takes a support-area or table card whose play sets off a draw or a look at the top of the deck (Old Toby by Gates of Isengard 103_121 or Southfarthing Leaf 17_110; 76 definitions use PlayCardFromDrawDeck). Reshuffle your draw deck.', the reshuffle after the play; on Q-0013 the printed reshuffle was called a habit of other Decipher games and redundant here.

name: Reckless Pride
summary: The definition word assignableToSkirmishAgainst counts a defender bonus that an assignment action cannot use. CR 4.2 'assignment phase': an assignment action assigns a minion to a companion only if "both of them are unassigned"; 'defender +X' is the Free Peoples player's own, when he assigns. The effect that assigns (AssignFpCharacterToSkirmish) rightly ignores defender, but the word a definition uses to ask "can this be assigned?" does not, so on a bearer with defender +1 who already has a minion a no-cost "Assign this minion to bearer of ..." (Reckless Pride 7_13 and its sisters, F-0353; the erratum 57_49) is still offered to another minion, is not flagged, and assigns nobody when used (Q-0034). The same code (Filters.assignableToSkirmish, gemp-lotr-logic) compares 1 + defender with the number of Assignment records naming the character, which is never more than 1, not with the minions he has: so the rig's FreepsCanAssign and FreepsCanAssignAgainst answer true for a defender +1 companion who already has his two minions. What the engine would have to do: have the definition word leave defender out when the Shadow player's side asks (as the effect does), and count minions where defender is counted.
found: at-mech-skirmish, lander: probed with Disquiet of Our People 2_2 making Gimli defender +1, Reckless Pride on him, two Uruk Savages; and converter: FreepsCanAssign read true after FreepsAssignToMinions(aragorn, troop1, troop2), though a third minion on him is refused.
outcome: Engine pass 24 (2026-10-10): the definition word assignableToSkirmishAgainst now asks what the AssignFpCharacterToSkirmish effect asks by default, through the flags the engine's own check already had (existing assignments counted, defender ignored, whichever player asks), so a no-cost "Assign this minion to bearer of ..." is no longer offered for a bearer who has a minion, defender or not; and where defender IS counted (the Free Peoples player's own assigning) the count is of the minions the character has, in one place (RuleUtils.hasRoomForAssignments) that the decision's handler, the decision's list of characters and the rig's FreepsCanAssign / FreepsCanAssignAgainst all ask. Went live: Card_07_013_Tests.WithItsBearerAssignedTheAbilityIsNotOfferedThoughHeHasDefender; four tests added to mechanics/DefenderTests and one to virtualtable/AssignmentReadingTests (G-0041 built with it). Ketura (2026-10-10): I believe the internal functions used for assignment checks have additional fields for flagging whether or not defender etc should be considered, for just this use case.  Likely the HJSON or test rig needs expanded to support the use of those flags.

name: Andúril, Flame of the West
summary: A card's 'when this is restored' trigger (the definition word `restored`) never answers a restore made by a reconcile, the commonest restore there is (CR 5.0 'reconcile': "When any player reconciles (before they discard any cards from hand), restore all cards owned by that player"). The cause: the trigger takes 'any' for its `source` when a definition writes none and then requires the restore to have a source card, and a reconcile's restore has none. What the engine would have to do: in trigger/Restored.java, make no source check when the definition gives no `source` (or let a restore with no source card pass 'any'). trigger/Hindered.java has the same default, harmless today because every hinder has a source card. name: Rivendell Waterfall
summary: Rivendell Waterfall 1_342, "While you can spot a ranger at Rivendell Waterfall, the move limit is +1 for this turn": a turn begun at the Waterfall with a ranger there gives no +1 if the ranger is dead by the time the site's check is carried out. Aragorn bears Blade Tip 1_209 and has 3 wounds; the turn begins at the Waterfall, the sanctuary heals are declined, and at the start of the fellowship phase "Required responses" lists the Waterfall's check beside Blade Tip. Blade Tip is taken first (the fourth wound); the next ordering lists Character death and Rivendell Waterfall twice; with the death taken first the check then does nothing, and the limit is 2 for the whole turn. With Rivendell Waterfall taken ahead of the death it is 3 (the regression test for #1091, whose own comment expects "exactly one extra move"). CR 4.2 'move limit': "If the move limit is modified for a turn, then that modification is in effect for the whole turn, even if the conditions for the modification change"; a ranger stood at the Waterfall as the turn began, so the turn has its +1 whatever order the Free Peoples player takes the required actions in. Until the check is carried out the limit also reads 2 (at the sanctuary-healing decision and through both orderings). The cause is in the engine: TriggerEffectProcessor, the isConstantCheck block written for #1091, gives every standing check a cost that runs source.isValid again as the check is carried out, so the standing condition (canSpot ranger) is looked at again as well as the once-a-turn limit the re-check was written for. That second look is right for a standing discard (F-0233, Q-0229: a card no longer where it may not be is not discarded) and wrong for a check that gives something for the turn. What the engine would have to do, one of two: (1) for a check that gives something for the turn, look again at carry-out only at what an earlier copy uses up (the per-turn limit) and not at the condition; (2) carry such a check out as it is collected and never put it to the Free Peoples player for ordering ("While" is continuous and no action: Rivendell Waterfall, and Silinde's copy of it, then leave the Required responses lists, and the limit no longer reads 2 while an ordering waits). The same build by a search of the definitions, none of them tried: The Number Must Be Few 1_260, Traitor's Voice 1_142, Sauron's Defenses 1_274, Bree Gate 1_327, Horse-country 4_326, Derndingle 4_330, Riding Like the Wind 11_155, Enraged Southron 12_64, Théoden 13_137, Race Text 91_8 and 91_12.
found: dec-b1_311, author: a test of the ranger dying ahead of the check, written to CR 4.2, read 2 where 3 was expected (the last reading; the board and both orderings read as expected before it). The reviewer tried it against the rules, the rulings (Q-0179, Q-0122, F-0333, F-0334) and the old #1091 test and could not knock it down. Lander: a probe took both orders on one board, 2 with the death first and 3 with the Waterfall first, and read 2 at the sanctuary decision and at both orderings.
outcome: Ketura (2026-10-11): Ehhh, this is a situation that is both so niche as to be a very diminishing-returns edge case, and also something that is 100% in the hands of the Free Peoples player who foolishly decided to choose the wrong order to resolve required triggers in.  I'm not worried about the timing on this; that's part of the reason *why* freeps has the last tiebreaking say in cases like this, so that it's their fault and not the rules.  Go ahead and drop this one. Open: an engine change, not made at landing. Parked on it: Card_01_342_Tests.TheMoveLimitIsRaisedThoughTheRangersDeathIsCarriedOutBeforeTheWaterfallsCheck. If the engine takes way (2), that test's two ordering steps go, and so do the two-entry orderings read in StartingATurnAtWaterfallWhileOtherTriggersResolveGivesOnlyPlusOne and in the Silinde test of the same file. Not corrected in the definition, though the reviewer showed a way: a second required trigger at the start of the fellowship phase beside the standing check, with the same requirements and the same two effects, makes the parked test pass (3 and never 4 in the three orders tried, and on a plain turn begun there). Left out because it mends one moment only (a turn begun there; not a move to the Waterfall or a ranger played there beside another required action), writes the effect twice, lists the Waterfall a third time in the ordering (the #1091 test's count of 2 becomes 3), and would be wanted on eleven other cards and taken out again once the engine is mended. It is ready if she wants it meanwhile. | DROPPED 2026-10-11 (her words above): no engine change is made; the parked test of 1_342 is deleted or cut to the game as built by engine pass 26, item `fixes`, and the card landed again. The item `turncheck`, which would have made the change, was void and did nothing. Done 2026-10-11 (engine pass 26, item fixes, commit dbd4a8ea5): the parked test is deleted and not cut down, since the half of the game as built (the Waterfall's check taken ahead of the death gives the +1) is already StartingATurnAtWaterfallWhileOtherTriggersResolveGivesOnlyPlusOne in the same file; nothing asserts that the other order should give it. name: Guarded Fastness
summary: A Free Peoples event that needs initiative to be played is counted toward its own initiative. CR 4.2 'playing a card': 'Reveal The Card from your hand, and it enters the void ... You cannot count The Card for initiative. ... If you are the Free Peoples player and initiative is a requirement for playing The Card, you must have four cards in your hand not counting The Card.' With exactly four cards in hand, Guarded Fastness 7_234 ('If you have initiative, discard 2 cards from hand to heal all [rohan] allies') among them, the event is offered and can be played: the haveInitiative requirement asks ModifiersLogic.hasInitiative, which counts the hand as it lies, the event still in it (and counts the void-from-hand while costs are paid). By the rule it wants four cards BESIDE itself. The same holds, by reading, for Stand to Arms 7_120, Where Shall We Go 7_78 and Charged Headlong 8_85; and the other way round for So Fair, So Desperate 8_111 ('If the Shadow has initiative, add a threat to ...'), which at four cards with itself among them should be playable (three beside it: the Shadow has initiative) and is not offered. An initiative that an EFFECT asks for is already read without the event (All Save One 7_31 played from four cards gives +2, not +4: the event is in the plain void by then), and an ability's requirement is checked before its cost (Madril 7_110): both are shown in mechanics/InitiativeTests.

outcome: Ketura (2026-10-11): I agree, A is the right choice. summary: A reinforcement could put its token on ANOTHER player's card. CR 4.2 'reinforce': 'You may choose any of your cards with the appropriate culture token if you have more than one.' The reinforceTokens effect chose among every active card that had a token of the culture asked for, and where no culture is named (Morannon Plains 18_137, 'each player may reinforce a culture token', the one such definition) among every active card with any culture token: on the move to Morannon Plains the Free Peoples player was offered the Shadow player's Ships of Great Draught beside his own conditions, and the Shadow player the Free Peoples player's Garrison of Osgiliath.
found: engine pass 26 (mech-c), writing mechanics/CultureTokensTests for Q-0220: C: a probe of Morannon Plains 18_137 with tokens on each player's cards ('Choose card to reinforce tokens on' listed both players' cards for each of them)
outcome: REVERTED (engine pass 28, item reverts, 2026-10-11): the Filters.owner(...) is out of ReinforceTokens' card resolver again, so a reinforcement is chosen among every active card with a token of the culture, either player's, as before engine pass 26. Shown by mechanics/CultureTokensTests.AtMorannonPlainsEachPlayerMayReinforceATokenOnACardOfEitherPlayers (Morannon Plains 18_137: each player is offered both players' cards, and each puts his token on the other's), which replaces APlayerReinforcesATokenOnACardOfHisOwnAndNeverOnAnotherPlayers. Not a bug until the rules council says: the issue is Ketura's to raise, and its answer may turn this round again. The revert also reaches the [gollum] culture, the one culture with token cards on both sides, which the first write-up missed (Q-0280). Ketura (2026-10-11): Hrrrm.  The full `reinforce` entry has a contradiction in it: "This verb, used in game text, means to add a culture token to a card that already has a token of the same culture. You may choose any of your cards with the appropriate culture token if you have more than one."  The first sentence reads as if there is no restriction on what side you choose, the second sentence implies you are restricted to only your own. I'm going to put a rules council issue in for this, but for now let's revert this and permit Morannon Plains to let either player choose either player's cards; there are some cards whose tokens "count up" and then self-discard upon accumulation (such as Scouring of the Shire), which is why someone might want the option to reinforce an opponent's card. Before that: mended for a day by engine pass 26 (mech-c), which held the choice to cards OWNED by the player who reinforces (CR 4.2 'reinforce': 'any of your cards').

summary: Site text while the starting fellowships are played (Ketura, 2026-10-10: 'I believe there was an earlier item that ensured that site text worked during starting fellowships ... we'll need to dig out that change and axe it'): there is no such change to axe. Shown on eight boards: at East Road 1_320 ('Each companion's twilight cost is +2') Gimli 2_121, Legolas 3_121 and Pippin 1_306 cost 2, 2 and 1 while each player chooses and Gimli and Legolas both go down, and Pippin costs 3 in the first fellowship phase; at Green Hill Country 1_323 Sam, Merry and Pippin cost 2, 1, 1 and fill the 4; at Edoras Hall 7_330 under Race Text 94_3 a [rohan] possession costs 1 in the choice and 0 once the game has begun; at Eastemnet Downs 4_324 a companion played into the fellowship asks no discard, and the same play in the first fellowship phase does; on a Shadows path East Road 11_236 the same, Trollshaw Forest 11_260 offers no draw for a possession played on a companion there (it does in the first fellowship phase), and Humble Homestead 13_152 played there at a dwelling site 1 takes no token for it (1 in the first fellowship phase): a site's keyword is not counted in that step either. The item she remembers is most likely G-0036 (engine pass 19), whose entry says a Shadows path 'start[s] at East Road with its text in force (Aragorn 1_89 costs 6 there)': that is the first fellowship phase, and it changed the test table only.

name: More Yet to Come
summary: More Yet to Come 10_3: 'If a Dwarf kills a minion in a skirmish and that minion did not take all wounds caused by that Dwarf's damage bonus, assign those remaining wounds to minions not assigned to a skirmish.' Where the Dwarf has beaten two minions and one dies with a wound over, playing the event also takes away the wound of his damage bonus that the OTHER loser was still to take. Gimli 1_13 (damage +1) beats a Goblin Runner (vitality 1) and an Uruk Savage together: the Runner dies of the first wound, the event puts its one remaining wound on a minion outside the skirmish, and the Savage ends with 1 wound. CR 4.2 'damage bonus' gives each loser its own ('each Orc takes two wounds'), the text speaks only of the wounds 'that minion' did not take, and with the event declined the Savage does take 2. The engine keeps ONE count of wounds still to place for all the losers of a skirmish (ResolveSkirmishDamageAction); killedWithSurplusDamage reads that count and consumeSurplusDamage sets it to 0. It would have to leave the rounds running for the losers still in play (the event taking only the killed minion's share out of them), or keep the count loser by loser. By reading, not run: two minions killed by the same wound each have a wound over by the text, and the event has the one count for the two of them.

summary: Rush of Steeds 11_157, "Response: If a minion exerts as a cost of its special ability, discard this condition to prevent that and return that minion to its owner's hand": the Response is also offered when a minion exerts as the EFFECT of its own special ability. Otherwise, exert this minion." In principle I'm fine with adding the cost flag to exert, but if the HDG is the only place this happens, we will defer until then to address it. No other card behaves differently: Rush of Steeds is the trigger's only user and the Giant the only minion whose own ability exerts it as an effect. name: Into the Caves
summary: Into the Caves 17_100: "Assign a minion to Frodo to make that minion lose all game text keywords of your choice ... until the regroup phase." A keyword named in one use of the card is taken again from the minion of every later use, though it is not named there, in that game and in every other game on the server: the first use names Easterling for an Easterling Axeman, the second (the fierce assignment of the same turn) names fierce alone for an Easterling Captain, and the Captain is no longer an Easterling. On a live server the card comes to strip every keyword anyone has named with it since the restart, whatever the player chooses. The removeKeyword effect keeps one set of keywords for the definition, and keywordFromMemory (a word this card alone uses) adds the named keyword to that set at every use (appender/RemoveKeyword.java: keywords.add(...) inside createEffect); the engine has to build a set for each use (the definition's keywords and the one named) and hand that to RemoveKeywordModifier. No definition mends it: nothing else takes a keyword from a memory.
found: dec-b17_100, author: a test that passed alone failed once another test of the file had named Easterling before it in the same JVM; the reviewer read the appender and ran the parked test alone, where it fails at its reading that the Captain is still an Easterling
outcome: Engine pass 28: RemoveKeyword now builds the keywords of each use afresh (the definition's own and the one named into memory) and never writes to the set the definition holds; a search of every appender for a use writing to what the definition holds found no other. Card_17_100_Tests.AKeywordNamedInAnEarlierUseIsNotLostByTheMinionOfALaterUse is live; 17_100 stays parked on Q-0282 alone.

name: Frodo, Weary From the Journey
summary: Frodo, Weary From the Journey 15_144 against Black Land Observer 15_101 (or Wandering Hillman 15_94), CR 4.2 "loops": 'When an infinite loop occurs that includes no voluntary actions, the loop ends immediately with no effect ... Neither the minions nor Frodo would get the strength bonuses.' The engine gives BOTH bonuses where the two texts loop. ModifiersLogic's recursion guard (_skipSet) works each modifier out with itself set aside, so each card sees the other without the other's bonus: Frodo at 9 before his bonus, skirmishing the Observer, is 11 against 11 and loses, where the rule has him 9 against 8 and winning (at 8 before his bonus: 10 against 11, the rule 8 against 8). There is no test of it, old or new: git history has none (searched every branch for the ids and titles); the probe is in engine pass 49's loop-proposal report.

Engine pass 50: ModifiersLogic now works a standing modifier out a second time, as if in force, when its own working out met it again for the same card, and leaves it out where that second answer undoes the first (CR 4.2 loops, no effect); Frodo 15_144 against Black Land Observer 15_101 and Wandering Hillman 15_94 at 8 and 9 before his bonus gets neither bonus, and the stable rows (7, 10, 11) read as printed. summary: A drawCards whose count is not a constant fails the game wherever the engine asks whether it can be done in full (a branch of a choice, as Hearth and Hall 17_8's 'draw a card for each hunter you can spot' was): DrawCards.isPlayableInFull reads the count with count.getEvaluator(null) and evaluateExpression(game, null), and a count such as forEachYouCanSpot needs the action context (NullPointerException).
